title: Distributional Shift in Monitors: Fine-tuning vs. Prompted Monitors Under Novel Task Types

original_idea.quick_reasoning: Clearly addresses an AI Safety problem with a reasonably scoped approach.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Practitioners must choose prompted vs. fine-tuned monitors. Robustness under distributional shift is a critical but unstudied factor. Clear practical guidance would result from this comparison.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Prompted monitor is simple, but fine-tuning a classifier on trajectory features requires ML pipeline setup, feature engineering, and training. Beginners with intro ML can do this with guidance but it adds substantial complexity.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Two monitor types, each evaluated on 10 held-out task types. Feature engineering, fine-tuning, and evaluation across many tasks is substantial. Could be narrowed to 5 held-out tasks to fit 30 hours.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: Novelty not assessed due to partial Wave 3 completion.
